subject: Reasoning
description: Statement → conclusion logic drills, banking/SSC high-hit

questions.stem: Statement: 'All government hospitals offer free services.' Conclusions: (I) Everyone uses government hospitals. (II) Some people prefer government hospitals for cost reasons. Which follows?
questions.explanation: (I) is too strong — 'all offer free' doesn't imply 'everyone uses'. (II) follows — if services are free, some people will choose them for the cost benefit. (II) is a reasonable inference, (I) is an over-generalisation.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'The company has decided to open factories only where uninterrupted electricity is available.' Conclusions: (I) Production requires continuous power supply. (II) The company will not open a factory in locations with frequent power cuts. Which follows?
questions.explanation: The decision implies BOTH (I) — the company believes continuous power is necessary — AND (II) — which is the direct logical restatement of 'only where uninterrupted electricity is available'. Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Attend the seminar — it will enhance your career prospects.' Which assumption is IMPLICIT?

options.option_text: The listener cares about their career.

questions.explanation: The speaker pitches the seminar as a career benefit — which only works as persuasion if the listener cares about their career. Other options either exaggerate (A — 'only') or bring unrelated details (C, D).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Regular exercise improves health.' Courses of action: (I) Encourage people to exercise daily. (II) Ban all unhealthy food products immediately. Which follows?
questions.explanation: (I) is a proportionate, directly relevant action. (II) is extreme and goes beyond what the statement justifies — the statement says exercise helps; it doesn't say food should be banned. Banking-style 'courses of action' questions reject disproportionate options.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'Some students of class X are toppers. All toppers are intelligent.' Conclusions: (I) Some students of class X are intelligent. (II) All students of class X are intelligent. Which follows?
questions.explanation: Some students are toppers, and all toppers are intelligent → those specific students are intelligent → 'some students are intelligent'. (II) is too strong — no statement supports 'all students'. Classic syllogistic pattern I + A → I.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'X Bank has the lowest interest rate on home loans.' Assumptions: (I) Home-loan customers compare interest rates across banks. (II) Lower interest rate attracts more home-loan customers. Which is implicit?
questions.explanation: Why advertise 'lowest interest rate' unless (I) customers compare and (II) lower rate attracts business? Both assumptions underlie the advertisement.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'India has the second-largest population in the world.' Conclusions: (I) Population is a significant resource for India. (II) China has a larger population than India. Which follows?
questions.explanation: (II) follows directly — 'second-largest' implies someone is larger. (China's rank here reflects the traditional textbook position; recent UN estimates show India may have overtaken China around 2023.) (I) is a value-judgement ('resource') the statement does not support.
